This integration connects Gladys to EnOcean devices — battery-free switches,
temperature, humidity, CO2, occupancy and light sensors, door contacts, window
handles, relays and dimmers — through an **ESP3 gateway**: the EnOcean USB 300
stick, a TCM 310 module, or any gateway built on them.

## 1. What you need

- Gladys **5.3 or later**.
- An ESP3 gateway (USB 300, USB 310, TCM 310 board...), for your country's
  frequency: 868 MHz in Europe, 902 MHz in North America.
- A machine on your network to plug it into: the Gladys host itself, or a
  Raspberry Pi closer to the devices.
- **ser2net** on that machine.

Why ser2net? The integration runs in a sandboxed container that cannot see
USB devices. ser2net shares the serial port of the stick as a TCP port, and the
integration connects to it. It also lets you put the stick where reception is
best, away from the Gladys server.

## 2. Share the stick with ser2net

Install it (`apt install ser2net` on Debian, Ubuntu and Raspberry Pi OS), then
find the stable name of the stick:

```bash
ls -l /dev/serial/by-id/
```

ser2net 4 (`/etc/ser2net.yaml`):

```yaml
connection: &enocean
  accepter: tcp,9999
  enable: on
  options:
    kickolduser: true
  connector: serialdev,/dev/serial/by-id/usb-EnOcean_GmbH_EnOcean_USB_300_DC_XXXXXXXX-if00-port0,57600n81,local
```

ser2net 3 (`/etc/ser2net.conf`):

```text
9999:raw:0:/dev/serial/by-id/usb-EnOcean_GmbH_EnOcean_USB_300_DC_XXXXXXXX-if00-port0:57600 8DATABITS NONE 1STOPBIT
```

Then `systemctl restart ser2net`. Keep in mind:

- **57600 bauds, 8N1, raw mode** (no telnet): ESP3 is binary.
- **`kickolduser: true`**: the port takes one client. When the integration
  reconnects (update, Gladys restart), the old session must give way.
- **The port has no password.** Open it to the Gladys host only: bind it to
  one address (`accepter: tcp,192.168.1.50,9999`) and/or filter it with your
  firewall.

## 3. Configure the integration

In **Integrations → EnOcean → Configuration**:

| Field                  | What to fill in                                                                  |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Gateway host           | IP address of the machine running ser2net. **Not 127.0.0.1** (own container).    |
| Gateway TCP port       | The port of ser2net (9999 above).                                                |
| Devices                | Your devices, see below.                                                         |
| Report unknown devices | Fires the "unknown device heard" scene trigger. Turn it off if neighbours flood. |
| Detailed logs (debug)  | Logs every telegram heard. For troubleshooting only.                             |

Save, then press **Test the connection**: it shows the module, its **base id**
and how many telegrams were heard.

## 4. Declare your devices

EnOcean has no discovery: a sensor says "I am 0194E3B2", never what it
measures. Each device is declared once, as a JSON list in the **Devices**
field:

```json
[
  { "id": "0194E3B2", "eep": "A5-02-05", "name": "Living room" },
  { "id": "FEF1A2B3", "eep": "F6-02-01", "name": "Entrance switch" },
  { "id": "01A1B2C3", "eep": "F6-10-00", "name": "Kitchen window" },
  { "eep": "A5-38-08", "channel": 1, "name": "Kitchen dimmer", "dimmable": true },
  { "eep": "F6-02-01", "channel": 2, "rocker": "a", "name": "Garden relay" },
  { "id": "05123456", "eep": "D2-01-12", "channel": 3, "name": "Plug" }
]
```

| Key        | Meaning                                                                                     |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`       | The EnOcean id of the device, 8 hex digits (printed on it). Needed for everything it sends. |
| `eep`      | Its profile (EEP), see the table below. Printed in its manual.                              |
| `name`     | The name shown in Gladys.                                                                   |
| `channel`  | Actuators only: the gateway channel (0-127) Gladys sends from. One per actuator or group.   |
| `dimmable` | `true` for a dimmer (A5-38-08, D2-01): adds a brightness feature.                           |
| `rocker`   | Virtual rocker relays: `a` (default) or `b`, the side the relay learned.                    |
| `io`       | D2-01 with several outputs: the output number (0 = first).                                  |

You do not have to read the ids yourself: open the **learn mode**, press the
button of the device, then press **Devices heard**. It prints the lines to
paste, with the profile when the device sends it.

After saving, the devices appear in **Discovery**: add them to Gladys there.

**Ids are forever.** Gladys keys the history, the scenes and the dashboards on
the `id` (sensors, D2-01) or on the `channel` (other actuators). Changing them
creates a new device.

## 5. Supported profiles

| EEP                       | Device                                       | In Gladys                                      |
| ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| A5-02-01 to 1B, 20, 30    | Temperature sensors                          | Temperature                                    |
| A5-04-01, A5-04-02        | Temperature and humidity sensors             | Temperature, humidity                          |
| A5-06-01, A5-06-02        | Light sensors                                | Illuminance (lx)                               |
| A5-07-01, 02, 03          | Occupancy sensors (03: with light)           | Motion (+ illuminance)                         |
| A5-09-04                  | CO2 sensors                                  | CO2, temperature, humidity                     |
| D5-00-01                  | Door and window contacts                     | Opening sensor (1 = closed)                    |
| F6-10-00                  | Window handles (Hoppe...)                    | Opening sensor + "handle turned" scene trigger |
| F6-02-01, F6-02-02 + `id` | Rocker switches (PTM 215, Eltako FT55...)    | 4 buttons (click / long click) + scene trigger |
| F6-02-01 + `channel`      | Relays that learned a rocker (Eltako FSR...) | On/off switch                                  |
| A5-38-08 + `channel`      | Eltako central command relays and dimmers    | On/off (+ brightness)                          |
| D2-01-00 to 14            | Electronic switches and dimmers (NodOn...)   | On/off (+ brightness)                          |

The buttons of a rocker switch are named after the EEP: `ao` / `ai` for the
upper / lower side of rocker A, `bo` / `bi` for rocker B. A press under one
second is a click, a longer one a long click.

## 6. Pair an actuator

Actuators are driven from a **channel** of the gateway: Gladys sends from the
gateway base id + the channel. The actuator must learn that sender once.

- **Relay that learns a rocker (F6-02-01 + channel)** and **Eltako central
  command (A5-38-08)**: turn the actuator to its learn position (LRN), then in
  Gladys press **Pair an actuator** and pick it. Turn it back to its operating
  position. Add the actuator `id` to the entry if you want Gladys to follow
  its confirmations (Eltako sends them).
- **D2-01 (NodOn...)**: they pair from their own side. Press **Open the learn
  mode** in Gladys (or the button of the widget), then the pairing button of
  the device: Gladys answers its request from channel 0, or from the channel
  already declared for its `id`. Declare it with its `id` and that channel
  (`0` when it was not declared yet).

The base id is burned into the stick. Keep the stick: with another one, the
actuators must learn the new sender again.

## 7. Scenes

Triggers:

- **An EnOcean switch is pressed**: filter on the switch, the button and the
  press (short, long). Variables: `device_name`, `button`, `press`,
  `duration_ms`.
- **A window handle is turned**: filter on the handle and the position
  (closed, open, tilted). Variables: `device_name`, `position`.
- **An unknown EnOcean device is heard**: once an hour per device at most.
  Variables: `sender_id`, `eep`, `rorg`, `dbm`, `teach_in`.
- **The EnOcean gateway is lost**: the TCP connection dropped (the integration
  keeps retrying). Variables: `address`, `reason`.

Actions:

- **Press a virtual EnOcean switch**: sends a rocker press from a channel,
  like a real switch. Every actuator that learned it reacts — handy for
  groups. Output: `sent`.
- **Send an EnOcean teach-in**: the teach-in telegram of a declared actuator.
  Output: `sent`.

## 8. Dashboard widget

The **EnOcean radio** widget shows the gateway state, its base id and module,
the learn mode, and the last devices heard (with their signal), the unknown
ones flagged. Its button opens the learn mode for 60 seconds.

## 9. Troubleshooting

- **"Gateway unreachable"**: check from the Gladys host that the port answers
  (`nc -vz 192.168.1.50 9999`), that ser2net runs, and that no other program
  (another home automation box) holds the port.
- **Connected but nothing heard**: wrong baud rate (57600), telnet mode
  instead of raw, or a stick of the wrong frequency.
- **A device is heard but nothing changes in Gladys**: wrong `eep` in its
  entry, or the device was not added from Discovery. Turn on the detailed logs:
  each telegram is logged with its sender and its bytes.
- **An actuator does not react**: it did not learn the channel (pair it
  again), or **Test the connection** says the base id is unknown.
- **Radio range**: concrete and metal walls block 868 MHz. Move the stick (a
  USB extension cable helps) or add an EnOcean repeater.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings EnOcean asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Getting started | `section` | No | The integration runs in a container that cannot see USB devices: plug your EnOcean USB 300 (or any ESP3 gateway) into a machine of your network and share it with ser2net as a raw TCP port at 57600 bauds. Then fill in its address below and declare your devices. |
| Gateway host | `string` | Yes | IP address or name of the machine running ser2net. Not 127.0.0.1: the integration runs in its own container. |
| Gateway TCP port | `number` | Yes | The port ser2net listens on for the EnOcean module (raw mode, no telnet). |
| Devices | `string` | No | Your EnOcean devices as a JSON list: one entry per device with its id (8 hex digits), its profile (EEP, e.g. A5-02-05) and a name. Actuators also get a channel (0-127). The "Devices heard" button writes the lines for you. See the documentation. |
| Report unknown devices | `boolean` | No | Fire the "An unknown EnOcean device is heard" scene trigger, at most once an hour per device. Turn it off if your neighbours' sensors are heard all day. |
| Detailed logs (debug) | `boolean` | No | Log every telegram heard, with its sender, its bytes and its signal. Turn it on to find out why a device does not show up, and off again once you know. |

## How to install EnOcean in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: EnOcean appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/prohand/gladys-enocean:1.0.1`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/prohand/gladys-enocean](https://github.com/prohand/gladys-enocean).

EnOcean requires Gladys `>=5.3.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

EnOcean is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [prohand](https://github.com/prohand), not by the Gladys core team.
